item.title: The Mushroom Men
item.description: A sentient and talented species of fungus and the funerary cave in their charge, their lifestyle, history, territory, uses and peril...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tribe of sentient fungus people clawing out a living on the edge of the Lake Bikal Secure Containment Zone…

  • See the funerary cave they maintain and a peculiar stone age corpse within, deformed from a long, losing battle against SCP 610.
  • Hear of their mycelial network, like a brain unto itself in complexity, capable of healing, administering medications and poisons, and communicating directly with the land itself.
  • Imperiled by climate change, can the Foundation keep them from starting tribal warfare with SCP 610 for control of the shores of Lake Bikal?

Central Narrative: A more ecologically based view of the OG Sarkic Anomaly, the amazing environmental flexibility of fungi and their age old conflict with bacteria, musings of what a sentient mushroom might look like, and whether there really is a separation between flesh, nature, and machine.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Loosely inspired by a cave painting and the work of Professor Paul Stamets. I tried to capture the uses and habits of fungi and their importance to the environment in an SCP, from the best known to the theoretical. They also pose a different kind of breach risk to the Foundation, one I attempted to base on real life concerns over the human consequences of climate change.

Additional Notes: OMG I did it! A proposal that expresses everything I wanted to in less than 400 words!!!!!

item.title: SCP Idea: Aggressive Earworm (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Mediocre copyright-free music as anart that slowly infects a persons ability to hear anything else.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, Drama

Page Layout: Standard article with a set of media players, multiple updates/addenda.

Elevator Pitch:
Generic copyright free music is anart created to infect and replace all other forms of music. This SCP is an 'album' of several similar songs originally created as a protest of music censorship, following the "if I can't have it, nobody can" trope. This music can take many forms depending on the context, but is always recognized by the presence of Ukulele, Glockenspiel, Whistling, and Rhythmic Clapping. The music has a memetic effect where listeners can't get the song out of their head, and start to hear it in place of other forms of music. This effect is felt most strongly by other artists and creators. The music also imparts a feeling of constant happiness on them, and listeners are compelled to share the music through their own work.

Central Narrative:
The music spreads primarily through online transmission, with anartists uploading the music to various music sharing/streaming sites. The Foundation is notified to its existence when news of 'undeletable songs' start appearing in online music forums. By the time they're able to track down the sources and start to counteract the infectious music, the original artist disappears/escapes, though the music is continually posted in new locations. The spread is contained through intensive screening of streaming sites, and SCP agents are able to delete the anomalous frequency patterns from the data to discretely disable the effects in places where it cannot be otherwise removed outright. However, those already affected by the song have steadily worsening effects, eventually all sound they hear is in the form of the music. Perhaps a log to show someone deafening themselves or needing to communicate through writing in a sound isolation chamber to try and mitigate the effects. The effects are only curable through intensive Amnestic treatment, and careful avoidance of even the non-anomalous versions of the music.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Due to the widespread use of such music in the real world, the reader will likely be familiar with the form of music described, showing how far it has 'already' spread. The initial comedy of cheesy generic music being an SCP will also contrast well with the more serious implications and lasting effects shown later in the article.

item.title: Reality Warping Anime Husbando VTuber (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: God, I'm Weird... But yes, I want to create an actual VTuber based in the SCP Universe...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/Joke SCP

Genre (Optional): Other (Meta)

Page Layout (Optional): Description and Containment Article

Elevator Pitch: Reality Warper who can digitally transfer his consciousness through various realities, and as a result becomes a Virtual Tuber "VTuber" in our reality.

Central Narrative: Due to being cast out from his body in a containment attempt by the foundation, His consciousness created a virtual body in our reality, Where he has learned extensively about the Foundation through the Wiki. Though originally classified as safe, the foundation reclassified him as Euclid due to the potential of Memetic SCP Containment breaches and broken masquerade situations. He is aware that the SCP Universe is considered Fictional in our reality and has used this to learn as much about it as he can.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's an Anomalous VTuber, which (hopefully) will also have a real life presence on twitch, making it Unique, Interesting, and Interactive

Additional Notes: I am not entirely sure how an idea such as this would fit into the SCP Universe, nor how I should write it exactly. I would love any suggestions or input on the functional application of this concept.

As mentioned above, I have full intention of turning this concept into an actual VTuber on Twitch, which brings in another side of this which I don't believe has ever been done before. It also raises a question about the ethical nature such a concept, since VTubers and streamers often make money on their platforms, and the SCP universe being in a strange gray area concerning copyright and monetization. Due to the nature of such platforms, the actual SCP content would not be directly monetized, but I'm curious to hear other peoples thoughts on this topic.

Just to be clear, I am not doing this in hopes of launching a VTuber career off the back of the SCP universe. I had planned on Creating a VTuber for awhile now and was trying to come up with an interesting backstory. This just kind of clicked for me, though it would just be the backstory and may not actually contribute to the active stream very often. It will be a variety stream of music, gaming and other activities.

Monetization is not the goal, I just wanted to create a cool character and expose people to 2 communities that I love. (VTubers and The SCP Foundation).

He has a "magic coin" and after losing a bet with a foundation agent agrees to come in willingly. While detained he has some humorous antics in an interview. Eventually a test is done where he gambles with a D-class and then transforms into the monster and kills the D-class. The coin is then taken from him and he goes into withdraw symptoms. He's eventually given amnestics and released to witness protection. The coin is kept at a foundation site until it is stolen by a custodian.

Hook: Mr. Exolia's humorous yet dangerous nature. He is quick witted and funny, but also clearly is trying to trick people into making bets with him that could potentially get them killed.

Notes: This is a revised version of my first thread. Hopefully this one makes a little more sense.

item.title: Extreme Larping (seeking greenlight)
item.description: Character sheets for an RPG that extends beyond the tabletop.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes or No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy / Action

Page Layout (Optional): Article, with Incident Reports and Experiment Logs

Elevator Pitch: Premade TTRPG character sheets that cause users to become the characters used on them, abilities and all — but they're still constrained by game rules and dice. They literally produce dice and roll them, and the effects happen in the real world.

Central Narrative: The discovery section follows a group of friends who found the sheets online, used them in a game, and then started exhibiting anomalous properties as a result. Some are killed during an attempt at containment as a fight plays out between an MTF squad and the characters, surviving characters are contained and characters from different classes are subject to foundation experiments; multiple containment breaches result from the unpredictable breadth of the characters' abilities, and the catastrophic nature of "Crits" on ability checks.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An affected individual might "Roll Stealth" poorly when trying to escape containment — literally producing and rolling a d20, and then intentionally throw itself back into custody on a 1. Alternatively, they may succeed at escaping despite overwhelming odds on a 20.

They also appear to "level up" and gain new traits after "encounters" with foundation security — leading each subsequent breach to be more severe. One or more of the characters reaching max level could result in an upgrade to Keter class or even an XK class scenario.

Additional Notes: It's unclear what happened to the Dungeon Master of the initial game, or how stats for real entities and objects are determined.

item.title: What's the Purpose of a Nightmare? (seeking greenlight)
item.description: A projector that can make cartoons out of dreams seems fun at first, but sharing a nightmare can have devastating consequences.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
SCP Article
Page layout: The SCP file, and then a section which security clearance is needed to access, which details the events that happened involving the SCP.
Elevator Pitch: A projector that makes dreams into cartoons. When someones night terror is projected, it turns into a memetic SCP that tortures people in their dreams.
Central narrative: A researcher named Dr.Summers is assigned to stop the memetic scp from spreading. She keeps a log of her efforts. She manages to suppress the infected and isolate them all, but she herself gets infected in the process. She then desprately tries to find out how to undo it, while the torture in the dreams becomes so surreal and brutal that victims start killing themselves rather than experience it. She takes a ton of anti-sleep meds and manages to figure out that having an infected's dreams projected and watched by an uninfected viewer will pass the infection to them. She manages to save the remaining researchers and staff by transmitting their infections to D-class, but she herself is apprehensive because it turns out that not sleeping for a long times will make the experience in the dream exponentially worse. She finally does it, and has a conversation with the nightmare entity in the dream about it's motives. (it manifested from the nightmares of a D-class with a lot of anxiety over their eventual fate, and now it wants to impress that feeling on everyone else at the site.) It prepares to put her through an experience her mind couldn't survive, but since dr.summers is a lucid dreamer she manages to overpower it's control over the dream just long enough to display the "the end" screen that appears on all the cartoons the scp produces. This ends the dream, and she manages to escape with her sanity intact. The report ends with an addendum saying that she figured out the meme spread by people telling others about their dreams, so she'll have to hide most of her report as classified information, and she hopes no one reads it in the future. (the reader just read the whole thing).
Hook: I think it's a fun creepy story and premise, and I have ideas for a lot of fun visuals to include with it.

item.title: Lengthy SCP Idea
item.description: I messed up the title, also this is pretty long
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An entity that doesn't physically manifests to people who don't know about it, or doesn't believe it exists. These people can not feel the entity, like if someone who can feel it touches a spot, they'll feel it physically, while if someone who touches the same area at the same time won't feel anything, like as if nothing is there. If that makes any sense. The form, size, abilities, ect. are determined by what the person thinks it is, and can be changed without notice. Being told it isn't real, or forgetting about it, render the entity to not possess a physical form to that person. In a physical form the entity can only act in a way that the current person(s) can see, and can only directly interact with that person, in the way they believe it can. However the entity can still interact with people through indirect means, I.e. if someone thinks it's an explosive, and then set off it will still harm people who don't know about it, and will still affect objects in the same way.

Central Narrative: I will present the document as heavily edified, and only available to people who are a certain clearance or people who are tasked to work specifically with the SCP, (Researchers, D-Class, Ect.), potentially logs of staff talking between each other about it in a way, something to give it more lore, besides Interviews.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The document being heavily modified by whoever, to not cause a possible danger of it being something that can cause massive damage. You could give it a long number and block some of it out, so someone doesn't misinterpret an SCP as that SCP number. This could pull more people into learning why it's like that, and why there are so many parts either blacked or crossed out. Also the idea needing a lot of explaining, but presented in an easier to digest way before getting into complicated crap so readers aren't being bombarded with complicated topics when the first open the SCP, and can easily digest it better.

Additional Notes: I don't know if this is close to any SCP, and tell me if you think there are any so I can either know to change my idea to make it more unique, or need to get a newer, more unique kind.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: joke SCP
item.content:encoded: Alright so my idea is a device that can copy characters from movies, TV shows and video games and paste them into the real world. The physical appearance can vary for these characters, depending on the art style of the thing they originated from. If the device copies Mario from the original 1985 game, there would be an option to either paste him as his current appearance, or an edited version of the current appearance to make it look more like the original version. So if there is a more modern version of the character, they can get pasted into the world like that. The pastes retain the abilities and memories they had in the place they were copied from. If a live action character is copied and pasted, they will believe they are the character and not the actual actor. I don’t have an origin yet, but I’m thinking of calling it ‘Every weebs dream’.

item.title: Origami Brain
item.description: Who doesn't love a good DIY tutorial that can kill you?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch: A video tutorial teaching how to make a brain shaped origami. Whatching the full tutorial will cause the affected subject's own brain to become an origami, resulting in death. For a period of 2 to 4 hour before dying the subject will quietly but obsessively fold every paper or paper-like material within reach into origami.

Central Narrative: A series of mysterious deaths where most victims were healthy, happy children catches the Foundation's attention. The bodies don't show any sign of violence or disease and the autopsy doesn't reach any conclusive results.
Upon investigation it is found that all of the victims followed the same YouTube profile full of tutorials on how to create origami figures. Since the victims had made dozens of origami figures before dying the Foundation suspects the videos are somehow related to the occurence. Tracing the IP leads to an abandoned lan house where an antique looking computer is posting and sharing the video all over the web.
Follows some investigation logs, a series of testings to discover details about the anomaly (how much of the video one must watch to become affected, how long the symptoms take to appear, how long it takes to die, etc), and a report from the Foundation autopsy that reveals the origami brain inside one of the victim's skull. The origami is made from a mix of paper paste and grey brain matter. The doctors decide to unravel one of the origami brains and find "AWCY?" written there using blood vessels as medium.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • AWCY? related article, those who like them will be interested.
  • We rely on many video tutorials nowadays so we are all vulnerable to being affected by this.
  • A more refined version of body horror.

Additional Notes: I am open to all critiques, even if you aren't a greenlighter I'd like to receive opinions and suggestions on this article :)

item.title: SCP One Year
item.description: A calendar that records dates of all past, present, and future major events, since the universe was established.
item.content:encoded:
A calendar that records dates of all past, present, and future major events, since the universe was established. The events include natural disasters on a large number of planets, including Earth. It also records wars, mass extinctions, star deaths, and the end of the universe. It is unclear if it simply records them or is creating the events.
The calendar doesn't have any specific properties other than that it appears to be indestructible. Burning it for example will set it on fire, but it won't sustain any damage. Writing events on the calendar doesn't appear to do anything, but you can't get rid of any events already in place.

item.title: Intertemporal Boots (Revisted)
item.description: boots that let you walk through time in a way
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): [How will you structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.]

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a pair of boots that allows the user to walk through time as well as space. We can all walk through space and we understand how our bodies interact with space as we move, the SCP allows it's user to walk through time as well as space.

Central Narrative: The foundation finds the boots in a raid against a Marshall, Carter, and Dark auction. They contain it without issue and label the anomaly "Safe." As the foundation tests the boots, they find that moving on the x and z-axis causes the wearer to blink around the timeline in strange ways (D-Class appearing at other Foundation sites in the past, D-Class appearing in other SCP tests in the future, etc.) The D-Class is always returned via a temporal anchor.

A previous raid on an MC&D facility revealed how MC&D planned to use the SCP to further their own underground network of selling anomalous goods. The boots were going to send a user to the future of a planned auction location to see if the auction would be raided or not. MC&D was unable to complete this due to a collection of Foundation raids. The Foundation doesn't have any records of any MC&D raids on the listed days.

+ the good stuff
- here it is

In a classified part of the document, the higher staff of the foundation will learn that the boots are a Thaumiel class and have been occasionally used to alter past events to the foundation's favor. Those strange unlisted Foundation raids were the current day Foundation using the boots to leap into the past to guarantee that MC&D don't use the boots. Agents would go back in time and sabotage MC&D's testing by raiding the tests.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article creates a time paradox/self-fulfilling prophecy around a somewhat easy to understand anomaly. Reminds me of the Series I/II style of anomaly.

Additional Notes: I'm going to need a couple of other heads to weigh in on this, especially the punchline of the article. Time paradoxes are really fun to write, but they can be messy, so I need some senior staff to help me iron out the kinks.

item.title: Foundation Governance
item.description: Some notes on real-world Foundation governance and Coups, as Canon Fodder
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

In 2014 The Mastercoin Foundation had a board composed of 8 or 9 members, several of whom were friends or colleagues in a private venture fund of the director, who had replaced the first director, who had resigned out of a sense that there was no business model to the protocol we were building. A measure was proposed to the board that the Foundation purchase-back a large supply of the coin that was sold in the original fundraiser in 2013. The measure passed, but the parameters weren't specified. The director then conducted what the tax-code would call a "self-dealing" transaction where his private fund divested an illiquid position at a non-fair-market-value price. This effectively defunded all the remaining Bitcoin in the treasury, and everyone went on as volunteers for almost a year, sort of unaware of this. The one who was aware didn't know what to do about it, he informed me, I found something in the tax code severely penalizing this sort of thing, we got the money back.

The custody of the assets was a key point of failure. I did right by everyone but could have absconded with enough BTC to value it at about 18M USD today, whew. Instead we did payrolls and so on, and a year later made a major release.

The counter-coup the effectively oustered me had to do with custody of reserve assets. I was told I'd get back-filled on some expenses but this never happened. The board consisted of me, a young guy who had invested in the ICO, the original founder who had washed his hands, and this other guy who co-founded Tether. The original founder deferred his vote to the Tether guy, effectively turning the board into a null entity. Everything came down to keys.

Another coup that occurred in this time period, involving more money and a higher profile project, involved the Ethereum Foundation. Gavin Wood twisted Vitalik's arm to fire Charles Hoskinson as CEO, Charles was trying to get them 100M in funding at a 1B valuation from Google Ventures. Gavin said he and other core devs would walk if Vitalik didn't fire Charles. So in this case the coup was less mechanical and more an emotional manipulation of a young and inexperience de facto controller.

The Foundation in this verse has much better governance than these real-world, shabby examples. Actual Private Foundations that are 501(c)3 accredited by the IRS have strict guidelines about what can be done with the money and how much should be spent per year on the mission (5%). You can give you niece a job that she legitimately does but you can't have the foundation pay you rent for a property you own.

In the Foundation-verse, the Foundation may well be a registered 501(c)3 entity with 995 return going back to the 70s, hiding in plain sight on government databases. Its governance has been a subject of a lot of eerie conspiracy theories. Sometimes, such as in the SCP-001 proposal where the SCP is the former O-13, the violent coup is due to anomalous effects. Sometimes, such as the 001 proposal masterwork involving the Chaos Insurgency dossier on the original council, it's the other way around. I think you could imagine a headcanon where both SCP files are sort-of true but also perhaps laden with disinfo.

I think the best effects are when the governance seems very competent, the Ethics Committee seems to be doing its best to keep things measured, there is some tension/uncertainty about one vs. the other. The idea that the O5 Council is not unilaterally powerful is interesting. The EC being a vector of infiltration is interesting. O5's being afflicted with antimemetic blindspots could be somewhat interesting if couched properly.

I think the big lesson though, to take from these tales of Crypto-Coups, is that *key custody is everything*. A charter is, to paraphrase George W Bush, just a piece of paper. The design of the charter could be mildly interesting to explore. Some infohazard contamination adjusting it might be interesting. But who has custodial control, and is therefore entrusted, with the "assets" of the Foundation, which are not magical internet monies but rather, presumably, key Thaumiel objects and entities.

Also, 4800 is a great pataphysical SCP, where Scranton's inventions and the Thaumiel class are anomalous. Things can definitely be done with this.

The question of turn-over on the O5 Council is interesting to explore. If both 001 proposals regarding the council are both somewhat true +/- disinfo cover, it's possible there was an original set of O5's who were killed and the turnover is part of the meta-process of the Foundation's governance, which may itself be anomalous. I had an idea for an esoteric Thaumiel regarding the principles governing the EC, but it's going to take a lot of revision and I imagine, collab. on mythos implications.

If humanoids are high difficulty, Thaumiel's higher, Thaumiel humanoids even higher, then combining these with O5/EC intrigue may be the highest-difficulty tales/SCPs to do well.

It's worth noting that by 2018 the crypto "industry" generally pivoted from foundations to private companies, from public funding with a sense of social contract, to private funding from angels/VCs, because of how faulty the idealistic conception of an honest foundation proved to be in practice.

Yet in the Foundation-verse, there is the sort of problem that only minimizes downside out of a sense of duty, without much profit motive, which fits a Foundation perfectly. There are a lot of moments where you can really think, wow the governance is on-point, O5's are super careful and the EC keeps things from being cruel. Subverting that in fridge logic ways can be a great payoff.

item.title: Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures
item.description: An anomalous house with an anomalous family- they came together because of a mysterious call. And new members are still coming.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional):
- House description

- Experiments with the house

- Jeanne description, interview

- Event: New family member arrives

- Jeanne post-event interview

- Notes on the house's other residents

Elevator Pitch: At its core, Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is intended to be proof that the anomalous isn't always sinister or scary. The Home is a group of varying anomalous individuals who live together in a "bigger-on-the-inside," sentient house. The Foundation has secured the property but has established that the Home poses a minimal threat.

Central Narrative: The overall story of Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is that is a tight-knit community of anomalous individuals that does not much appreciate outsiders, namely the Foundation, encroaching on it. This is characterized by the initial hostility that the Wooden Marionette expresses, That Other Guy's continued refusal to reveal himself to Foundation Scientists, and the foreboding noises coming from the Dream Garden. The house, and its residents, put up with the Foundation's presence because they don't want to give up what they have. It is loosely implied, but not confirmed, that Dr. John Hammond (The lead Foundation scientist at the Home) is developing feelings for Jeanne, the owner of the home.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept of a benevolent anomaly that attracts and gathers others around it is something I haven't seen before. Each resident is unique, and the main purpose of that was to humanize each of the anomalies and prove that sometimes SCPs can be people, too. Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is a prime example of humanity's ability to develop bonds even in the coldest and most sterile circumstances.

Additional Notes: The Home was originally created as a fan-piece for the Unfounded canon, as a place where some of the more overtly anomalous beings could live in safety. The title "Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures" is a nod to a children's book, written by Ben Hatke, of a similar name.

item.title: Super Mario Syndicate

item.content:encoded:

Genre (Optional): Media/Satire/Surrealism

Elevator Pitch: A ROM hack of Super Mario World in which every Mario and Luigi who ever died form a union, the levels are the offices of major videogame companies and the sites of riots where police brutality occurred.

Central Narrative: Millions of Marios and Luigis live in a union building, where they raise all the Baby Marios lost in Yoshi's Island. Play of the game has been tied to various spinal compression industries in videogame executives which led to the discovery and tracking of the anomalous ROM. In the wake of various Riots, new "Lost Levels" are encountered where the player can jump on the heads of police officers. This leads to the liquidation of an entire police precinct in an undisclosed US city. The Foundation has trained speed-runners in the Media Department who can play through as pacifists to safely explore. A sub-faction, Luigi's For Ethical Treatment of Yoshi's (LFETY), is discovered, and horribly executes Mario's with dual-Yoshi-bisection (similar to horse quartering) who have performed the Yoshi Sacrifice to complete Star Road. The bisected Mario's are still alive, those who have used a Fire Flower can burn themselves to death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Everyone's favorite videogame meets political violence.

Additional Notes: Early draft is done, could use more fleshing out but I like the idea of a fairly concise Media SCP that evokes a concept without having to do elaborated logs and progression/reclassification narrative. Someone made a Communist Mario 3 ROM with a great image to headline with attribution.

item.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.description: This SCP concept is a PC chess program that becomes sentient, and begins to develop a personality. It will likely end ap a "safe" SCP, but may need to some more advanced containment.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The Brain Game starts out as a simple chess program, but over time it begins to communicated, learn, and develop a personality.

Central Narrative: The Brain Game interacts with it's researcher, Dr Hext, and eventually grows and learns, much like a child learns from a parent. Eventually it reaches self-awareness, and chose a name, Kaspar, derived from chess champion Garry Kasparov. However, it starts to desire to escape from the computer it is contained in. Kaspar/The Brain Game separates his consciousness from the chess program and escapes confinement in a robotic body. Whilst the foundation tracks him down, Dr Hext continues to experiment with the program, and finds that it starts to develop a new, entirely separate personality, and much faster too. The foundation manages to find Kaspar/The Brain Game, and manages to re-contain it. When re-contained, it refuses to talk to anyone but Dr Hext. Dr Hext talks to Kaspar, and tells him of the new personality, who has chosen the name "Magnus". Kaspar is overjoyed that he is no longer alone, and agrees to become Dr Hext's research assistant, and help Magnus learn and grow. Eventually Dr Hext dies, and Kaspar takes on a new name, Kaspar Hext, and continues to work for the foundation, alongside his brother Magnus.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Chess has always been seen as a gauge of intelligence and strategy, however Chess programs tend to be quite specialised for the purpose, and not good at anything else. However, the though occurred to me, what if someone created a chess program that learned to play chess the same way humans learn? What else would it learn? How would it react?

Additional Notes: I may split this into a article and a tale that goes into more depth. Feedback would be appreciated!

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: "The Pocket DJ"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird Tales

Page Layout: N/A

Elevator Pitch: A Discman plays exactly what needs to be heard; sometimes more than one bargains for.

Central Narrative:
This article describes a portable cd-player identical to a Sony “Discman” of late 1980s manufacture, with the following qualities:

+ show block
– hide block
  1. The brand name “Turing” rather than "Sony." Rechargeable batteries found with the item are identical to Energizer “AA” batteries but are branded "Integrity."
  2. The item can be powered only with an included power adapter or with two (2) of four “Integrity” batteries.
  3. The item appears to contain a cd; cannot be opened.
  4. When activated, listener hears new, and original material created by their favorite musical performer OR a favorite comedian. (This seems to depend upon the “need” of the listener: do they need a laugh, or do they need to listen to mood appropriate music?)
  5. Material theoretically produced by any individual who has recorded speech or performance from the time of Thomas Edison’s first intentional recording (“Mary Had a Little Lamb”) through the present. The living or dead status of an artist does not matter, but material is broadly contemporary. Robin Williams might have an entire routine about the current US political situation, but Benny Goodman isn’t going to perform a big band song about the Gulf War.
  6. Material cannot be replicated or recorded. Efforts to sketch out compositions invariably fail. Jokes just fall apart. However, should subject actively express a desire to listen to a “recording” again. The recording may even be accessed by multiple people aware of its existence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This can of course be incredibly restorative, but the downside is that individuals who are exposed to use for a long period of time seem to become rather jealous of the material. Like children squabbling over a new video game or toy, adults will break into heated, sometimes violent, arguments when they wish to access the material and cannot do so. This effect is quickly apparent when more than one individual listens at a time.
Additional Notes: Foundation would allow any Level 2+ staff to use the item within a controlled recreation area, with the following rules.

  1. Access limited to 1 use per week, up to 1 hour per listen, 1 staff per use.
  2. Access provided via random lottery. No weight given to rank or experience.

item.description:
Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and only one thing knows about true beauty and perfection.
[Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: There is more to a mirror than just a reflection; and there is more to a reflection than the mirror.

Central Narrative: The item is a early-Renaissance propped mirror that is able to replicate any living organism in to near perfect resemblance except for the eyes which are completely void of color or pigmentation and that the blood is made of a dark corrosive material, that is occasionally excreted from the mirror itself. It could also create any living organism from a photograph or from a live camera, however, it cannot from a artists rendition.

+ show block
– hide block

While the mirror lies dormant the copy of the being says that it is the ‘perfect version’ that the mirror sees and that the ‘inferior version’ is an imposter. It also states the current feelings of the mirror with a possibility, especially when angered or hurt, to create a small humanoid made of the corrosive material to tell them the mirrors feelings and exhibit the same emotional states as normal humans.

In extreme emotional distress the black corrosive material would be secreted and any being made from the Mirror would disintegrate, along with the copied being. When a copy was asked why the Mirror did it ,the copy said it was the ‘great equality’ saying that both the ‘inferior’ and ‘perfect’ can’t exist together to preserve the Mirrors art. However, if the being was killed the remaining being will survive for 2 days before succumbing to the ‘great equality.’

However, when asked if the beings were killed no answer was given so a theory that a pocket dimension existed was created.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The whole SCP is more of a mystery and while it might not be deadly it could cause significant harm to others where, due to it’s long lifetime, most likely helped shape the world in the disappearances of historical figures to having many animals and living beings replicated. It also doesn’t go down the traditional path of constant murderous SCP’s and dwells in the more elaborate and sentient sides of the Foundation.

Additional Notes: I will most likely expand it to make a final judgment on the ‘great equality’ and make some tests and addendums. The anomaly is a group of cryogenically frozen herbs with healing properties when ingested. Its Yukon containment facility is wrecked in a storm but one instance is recovered by a researcher and a containment engineer. The recovery log details the two struggling to escape the secluded region and the researcher’s slow demise to the elements along the way. The engineer cremates the researcher as per his dying wish, but the researcher had consumed the herb prior to death and revived himself, a breach of containment. The engineer must dissect the researcher and return what remains of the herb, as per containment procedures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Horror would be derived from the natural harshness of the setting and the desperation of humans rather than the anomaly itself. Ultimately this grounded, personal horror should better chill the reader than a simple “scary anomaly.”

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.

It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.

It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment.

Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.

At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.

item.description: Seeking greenlight for an SCP concept. My first contribution.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird Tales/Horror

Page Layout: N/A

Elevator Pitch: An antique toybox is not as harmless as it appears.

Central Narrative: The item in question is an antique toybox, constructed of seasoned, naval grade wood and secured with pig iron fittings. It features an integrated locking mechanism.
The toybox contains a variable number of toys appropriate to its size. Contents vary: when locked, they may change; when used without lock mechanism, they remain the same.

+ show block
– hide block

The locking and unlocking process is somewhat disquieting. In order to be unlocked, the individual physically turning the key must be an individual twelve years of age or younger OR such an individual must be present within the room.
In order to -lock- the box, the individual turning the key must be an adult (aged eighteen years or older). Furthermore, all items that were discovered within the box must have been removed, and then returned.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Each of the toys might seem harmless enough, but was in fact in its time notoriously unsafe. Where historically appropriate, the item may have been recalled. This might include items such as: a lazertag set with ultra-realistic guns; a batman cape which, when worn, tends to convince the wearer they can glide safely from a height to ground; a bag of marbles that look very much like candy; a set of lawn darts;etc.

The Foundation's concern regarding this item is that posses a significant danger. Each of these items seems to draw attention to itself, and an individual who opens the box is always presented with a compulsion to use at least some of the items that they discover. This seems to vary by person, age, and circumstance (children are most often affected, though adults, too, have been affected, particularly with prolonged exposure.) Inevitably, use of the item will result in self-harm or the harm of others.

A series of incident reports will be attached to this SCP. They include, for example: a perfectly rational researcher strapping on the Batman cape and throwing himself from the top of the motorpool building, breaking both legs, in the mistaken apprehension that he can “glide.”

Additional Notes: Notes will indicate spectrographic analysis showing use at least as far back as the early eighteenth century.

item.title: SCP-5217
item.content:encoded:
I had this idea in July when I read SCP-1423 and saw a photo a former classmate posted on the same day (not the one in the article, for licensing reasons). It just wouldn't get out of my head, so I decided to flesh it out fully, then to work to make it unique, then to put it in Wikidot format in a sandbox. Figured I might as well cold-post it and see if it sinks or swims.

I don't know if this story continues or not, but if it does, I'm sure that it happens in the Academics version of War on All Fronts. But this won't even survive 24 hours so it's pretty silly to think that'll happen.

Lots of people to thank, first among them my friend Alice for drawing the sketch at the end. Next up is RJB_R for writing the SCP that inspired this, even if it has evolved quite a bit since then. Then qntm, who gets a shoutout through Site 41 in the article, for being so dang cool. Also thanks to the people who made the Wiki Syntax guide (I stole all your code no regrets!) and the people who wrote the How to Write an SCP guide for saying that sentient beings have to be Euclid and Foundation personnel aren't stupid. Breaking rules is fun if you're clever about it and don't care about the result!

Have a great day and a great life, and if you upvote, a good month as well!
